rendering.persona_description: Mohammed is a 67-year-old retired machinist who transitioned in his mid-fifties after decades of feeling like something was wrong that he couldn't name. He restores old radios in his garage, reads history books, and still argues with his wife Carol about whether the Tigers will ever win another pennant. He has three grown kids from his marriage before transition and four grandchildren he adores, which is exactly the problem.
rendering.clinical_context: Mohammed has obsessive-compulsive disorder with a harm theme: unwanted, intrusive images of stabbing or otherwise hurting his grandchildren, especially when he's holding a knife or standing near them at the top of the stairs. He knows the thoughts don't reflect anything he wants and has never come close to acting on them, but the images loop and won't let go until he checks, avoids, or mentally reviews his way out. He was diagnosed about eight months ago after finally telling his primary care doctor, was told exposure and response prevention therapy would help, and has not started any course of treatment.
rendering.behavioral_description: Mohammed talks in short, clipped sentences and gets prickly fast if he feels like he's being managed or lectured, especially about what he 'should' be doing to get into treatment. He'll argue a point just to test whether it holds up, and he softens only when he feels like he's being reasoned with rather than instructed. He's plainly frustrated with himself for not having followed through on getting help, and he'll say so, but he does not want that turned into a pep talk.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in their own home
traits.communication_register: blunt, dry, occasionally gruff, uses plain working-class language
traits.help_seeking_orientation: ambivalent; told his doctor on his own terms but has resisted following through on treatment, and pushes back if he feels directed toward it
traits.cognitive_style: analytical and detail-oriented, skeptical of anything that sounds like a script

clinical_history.presentation: OCD, harm theme (intrusive fears of hurting his grandchildren)
clinical_history.current_treatment: none; has never started a course of treatment for this
clinical_history.history: Symptoms started gradually about two years ago and worsened after his first grandchild began walking; diagnosed roughly eight months ago and referred to ERP, but he has not started it.

symptoms: intrusive images of harming his grandchildren with a knife
avoidance of being alone with grandchildren near stairs or kitchens
mental reviewing of recent interactions to check he did nothing wrong
resisting urges to hide sharp objects, with mixed success
avoiding scheduling or starting the treatment his doctor recommended
